title: Maximum product influence
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega)\to\mathbb{R}$. The maximum product influence of $f$ is the largest of its coordinate product influences when $n>0$, and is zero when $n=0$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$f$ is a real-valued function on $\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega$
